summary_paragraph: A woman with a complex medical history including sclerosing mesenteritis, chronic abdominal pain, and long-term TPN dependence via a femoral catheter was admitted for chills and suspected infection. She was found to have Pseudomonas bacteremia from her central line, which was removed and replaced. During her hospitalization, she completed a course of antibiotics, and repeat blood cultures remained negative. Nutrition assessment confirmed adequate oral intake, leading to discontinuation of TPN and eventual removal of the femoral line. Her vitamin D and calcium deficiencies were addressed with supplementation, and her mental health concerns were supported by psychiatry. She improved neurologically after sedating medications were temporarily held. She was discharged home with a plan to continue oral nutrition, monitor weight, and follow up with endocrinology, GI, and pain management for ongoing care.
